A newer version of both had just landed moments earlier, so this undoes that move and returns to the prior stable versions. If you use the assistant today, you will not see any visible difference in what it can do, but the underlying plumbing that keeps it running is back to the version the team had already tested and shipped.

Scope covers `.agents/` definitions, backend API handlers, and `backend/package.json`.

eli5.text: When you build or use an AI assistant built on this platform, the way you tell that assistant to run tools (like searching the web or reading files) has changed: instead of labeling the information you pass to a tool as 'args', it is now labeled 'input'. This affects everyone who writes or uses agent definitions, because every tool call they configure will use the new label, and older references to the old label would break. Behind the scenes, the underlying AI and validation libraries were also upgraded to newer versions, which is why the argument label had to change.

Now, those strict brevity rules are selectively applied only to older model versions, giving the newer model room to provide fuller explanations when needed. This means outputs from the newer model should feel less aggressively compressed and more complete, particularly for intricate coding work.

eli5.text: A new helper named "Mitt the Git Committer" is now available inside the development toolkit. When a developer asks it to save changes, it runs Git commands to review what changed and the recent commit history, reads any relevant files, then stages the right files and writes a commit message in the standard format with the Codebuff footer. The helper is defined and ready to use today, so developers can simply request a commit and let it handle the review and saving steps automatically.

ai.title: SDK runterminalcommand tool added
ai.summary: SDK client now implements `run_terminal_command` via new `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` using `child_process.spawn`. Replaces previous throw with synchronous execution supporting `SYNC` mode, timeout handling, and combined stdout/stderr output. `handleToolCall` response structure updated to `output: { type: 'text', value }` shape.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to run a terminal command (like listing files or checking status), it can now actually do it instead of saying it cannot. The command runs on your machine in your project folder, captures both normal output and errors together, and stops automatically if it takes too long. You get back a single block of text showing what the command printed.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.8 adds run-state helpers for images and history
ai.summary: Version 0.1.8 introduces `generateInitialRunState`, `withAdditionalMessage`, and `withMessageHistory` in `sdk/src/run-state.ts` to inject images, files, or modify message history before execution. These replace the exported `getInitialSessionState` and internal `initialSessionState` logic previously hidden in `client.ts`. The `CodebuffClient` now accepts a constructed `RunState` via `previousRun`, enabling multimodal prompts (e.g., image URLs) in `README.md` examples. `index.ts` exports the new functions, deprecating direct session state creation.

eli5.text: Developers building desktop apps with the Codebuff SDK can now attach images and other files to prompts, and reshape the conversation history before a run happens. Under the hood, helpers like `generateInitialRunState`, `withAdditionalMessage`, and `withMessageHistory` replace the previously hidden session-state setup inside the client. You'd notice this if you're wiring up multimodal prompts (e.g., feeding an image URL into an agent question); the sample walkthrough now shows an agent analyzing an attached image. Live today with SDK 0.1.8.

ai.title: Stabilize researcher readdocs tests via mock verification
ai.summary: Refactor `backend/src/__tests__/read-docs-tool.test.ts` to stabilize researcher agent tests. Added mock tracking for `analytics`, `websocketAction`, and `liveUserInputs` to prevent hangs and ensure proper cleanup. New tests verify mock implementations and async generator completion. Replaced functional `read_docs` scenarios with infrastructure validation to isolate test flakiness.

eli5.text: The team replaced the actual step-by-step checks that test the help-document tool with a fake version, so the tests no longer wait around for slow real steps to finish and they clean up properly afterward. You wouldn't see this change yourself, but it means the automated checks behind the scenes are more reliable and faster now, with fewer random failures.

ai.title: Replace :fast tag with :nitro in open-source model definitions
ai.summary: Open-source agent definitions and `ModelName` types now use the `:nitro` suffix instead of `:fast`. This applies to Qwen, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Z-ai models across `.agents/opensource/` and `common/src/templates/`. The change ensures consistency with upstream model naming conventions.

eli5.text: The open-source AI assistants bundled with the software now talk to a different version of certain models from Qwen, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Z-ai. Specifically, any model reference that previously used the tag:fast now uses:nitro instead, matching the naming those companies use upstream. If you looked at the configuration of any of these assistants (for example, the coder, researcher, reviewer, thinker, file-picker, or base agents), you would see the model name ending in:nitro rather than:fast, and the list of supported model names in the type definitions would reflect the same swap. ai.title: Update reviewer agent model to gpt-oss-120b:nitro
ai.summary: The reviewer agent definition in .agents/reviewer.ts now uses openai/gpt-oss-120b:nitro instead of openai/gpt-5. This internal change updates the model string passed to the reviewer helper function. The scope is limited to the agent configuration file.

eli5.text: The automated code-review assistant will now be evaluated by a different, newer AI model when it checks pull requests. If you look at the reviewer agent's behavior today, you may notice slightly different wording or a different focus in the review comments it leaves, because the underlying model that generates those reviews has swapped. This only affects the internal model used by the reviewer agent; everything else about how reviews are triggered and reported stays the same.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.467
ai.summary: The version number for the codebuff package in npm-app/release/package.json is updated from 1.0.466 to 1.0.467.

eli5.text: This release updates the package to version 1.0.467, which includes several new capabilities. You can now use a file picker powered by a newer, more capable AI model, and the assistant gains a new step-by-step prompting feature for complex tasks. The system also adds a new validation step that checks agent IDs before they run, and it now requires an API key to confirm your identity during agent setup. Additionally, a new terminal command tool is available in the SDK, along with helper functions for handling images and conversation history. Some older model setups were updated or replaced with newer alternatives.

ai.title: Add closeConnection method to CodebuffClient
ai.summary: CodebuffClient gains `closeConnection` method. Invokes `websocketHandler.close` to terminate connections. Scope: `sdk/src/client.ts`, `sdk/README.md`, `sdk/CHANGELOG.md`. Bumped version 0.1.9.

eli5.text: When you use the Codebuff coding assistant inside your project, it keeps a live connection open to send you suggestions. After this change, you can now tell that connection to shut down cleanly instead of just walking away, which helps your computer close things out properly. If you looked at the instructions, you'd see a new line in the examples showing this clean shutdown step being called right after a coding task finishes. The feature is live today and works any time you use the assistant.

ai.title: Update validate-agent-name.test.ts
ai.summary: Test mocks for validateAgentNameHandler now include x-codebuff-api-key headers by default. Added coverage for 403 API key required errors on missing headers. Scope limited to backend/src/api/__tests__/validate-agent-name.test.ts. Ensures handler auth checks remain verified in test suite.

eli5.text: The system now requires a valid API key before it will even check if an agent name is taken. Previously, the name-check tool would respond even without a key; now requests missing the key get blocked with a clear 'API key required' message before any other work happens. This raises the bar for who can call that name-check tool, so unauthorized callers are turned away earlier in the request.

ai.title: Switch reviewer agent model to qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507
ai.summary: Internal reviewer agent configuration updated in .agents/reviewer.ts. Model identifier changed from openai/gpt-oss-120b:nitro to qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507:nitro. This affects the code review automation logic only.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that checks code for problems is now using a different AI model to do its work. This is a behind-the-scenes change that only affects how the automated review system evaluates code; it does not change what gets reviewed or how developers submit code. You would not notice anything change in your workflow, since it's a configuration tweak inside the review tooling.
